sources.title: BMW Canada further improves EV convenience in Canada with Shell Recharge integration and access to NACS-format Superchargers (2026-04-08)
sources.notes: Supercharger access from 2026-04-08 per vehicle via remote software upgrade; CCS-port cars need the approved Lectron Vortex Plus NACS-to-CCS adapter; only all-new models sold in Canada from 2026 (iX3, i3) get a built-in NACS port. Page does not name the i4 in the text read; the model list was seen in a search excerpt.

sources.title: Motor Illustrated: Should you buy a 2026 Volvo EX30?
sources.notes: Canadian review of the 2026 EX30 (Core, Plus, Ultra, Cross Country AWD): CCS1 charge port, 153 kW peak DC, 11 kW onboard charger. No mention of NACS.

supercharger_access.notes: BMW Canada (2026-04-08): CCS-port BMW BEVs get Supercharger access via RSU and the approved Lectron Vortex Plus NACS-to-CCS adapter; the i4 keeps its CCS1 port (native NACS only on all-new 2026+ models such as iX3, i3). US access began 2025-12-10 (BMWBlog lists i4).

charge_port.notes: Estimated: thinkEV's 2026 i4 page states CCS1 in the eDrive40 spec table (it gives only range figures for the other trims); same model, generation and year, and BMW's 2026 native-NACS list (BMWBlog, BMW Canada) does not include the i4.

supercharger_access.notes: BMW Canada (2026-04-08): CCS-port BMW BEVs get Supercharger access via RSU and the approved Lectron adapter. i4 listed by BMWBlog for the US (2025-12-10).

charge_port.notes: Estimated: thinkEV's 2026 i4 page states CCS1 in the eDrive40 spec table (it gives only range figures for the other trims); same model, generation and year, and the first native NACS BMW is the 2026 i5 M60 (BMWBlog), not the i4 M60.
